en.name: Horseradish, jarred
en.summary: Jarred horseradish is grated root held in vinegar, and it is sold from the chilled cabinet because it belongs there. From purchase it keeps about 12 months refrigerated unopened, and about 3–4 months once opened. Heat, not spoilage, is what it loses first.
en.pantry: Prepared horseradish is not a cupboard product. The pungency that makes it worth eating comes from volatile compounds released when the root is grated, and they dissipate steadily — faster in a warm room, and faster still in the light. There is no room-temperature timeline to give; keep the jar cold from the shop to the fridge, and put it back after every use rather than leaving it on the table through a roast dinner.
en.fridge: Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below on an inside shelf, not in the door. Unopened it runs about 12 months from purchase; opened, about 3–4 months. Keep the lid tight — air is what flattens the heat — and use a clean dry spoon, never one that has been on a plate. The colour will darken from bright white towards beige as it ages, and the sharpness fades with it; a jar that no longer makes your eyes water is past its useful life even if nothing is wrong with it.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for jarred horseradish and freezing does not preserve the thing you actually want. The heat is volatile, and freezing and thawing drives it off while leaving a watery, separated paste behind. If you want horseradish on hand for months, the practical route is to keep a whole root in the fridge and grate what you need, since the intact root holds its pungency far better than any grated product.
spoilage: A dark brown or greyish colour with no white left
No heat at all on the nose or the tongue — old rather than unsafe
Mould on the surface or around the rim
A rotten or fermented smell, or liquid separating with a foul edge
tips: Buy the smallest jar you will finish; potency is the real clock here.
Keep the lid tight and the jar on a cold inside shelf, not the door.
Use a clean dry spoon and never return sauce from the table.
Stir in horseradish at the end of cooking; heat destroys the pungency.

faq.q: How long does jarred horseradish last once opened?
faq.a: About 3–4 months refrigerated at 4 °C or below. Unopened, about 12 months from purchase.

faq.q: Does horseradish need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Yes. It is sold chilled and belongs in the fridge, unopened and opened alike.

faq.q: Why has my horseradish lost its heat?
faq.a: The pungent compounds are volatile and escape over time, faster once the jar is opened and faster still if it is left warm.
There is no timeline and it does not work well — freezing drives off the heat and leaves a watery paste. Keep a whole root in the fridge instead.

zh.name: 瓶裝辣根醬
zh.summary: 瓶裝辣根醬是磨碎的辣根泡在醋裡，它放在冷藏櫃販售，因為那本來就是它該待的地方。從購買日起算，未開封冷藏大約 12 個月，開封後大約 3～4 個月。它最先失去的是辛辣，而不是安全性。
zh.pantry: 調製好的辣根醬不是常溫商品。它之所以好吃，靠的是磨碎時釋出的揮發性成分，而這些成分會持續散失——室溫越高散得越快，照到光更快。這裡沒有常溫天數可以給；從賣場到冰箱都要保持低溫，每次用完就放回去，不要讓罐子在一整頓烤肉大餐的餐桌上擺著。
zh.fridge: 請放 4 °C 以下的冰箱內側層架，不要放門邊。未開封從購買日起算大約 12 個月；開封後大約 3～4 個月。蓋子要蓋緊——讓辛辣消失的是空氣——並使用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，絕對不要用剛從盤子上拿起的那支。它會從雪白逐漸轉成米黃色，嗆勁也隨之減弱；一罐已經嗆不出眼淚的辣根醬，即使沒有壞，也已經失去使用價值。
zh.freezer: 瓶裝辣根醬沒有冷凍期限，而且冷凍保不住你真正想要的東西。辛辣成分是揮發性的，一凍一解就散掉，留下的只是出水分離的糊。想常備好幾個月的話，實際的做法是冰一整條辣根、要用時現磨，因為完整的根保留嗆勁的能力遠勝任何磨好的產品。
spoilage: 顏色轉成深褐或發灰，完全看不到白色
聞起來、吃起來都完全沒有嗆勁——那是老了，不是不安全
有腐敗味或發酵味，或分離出的液體帶異味
tips: 買你吃得完的最小罐；這裡真正的時鐘是嗆度。
蓋緊，並放在冰箱內側冷的位置，不要放門邊。
用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，桌上剩的絕不倒回去。
辣根醬要在起鍋前才拌入；加熱會破壞嗆味。

faq.q: 瓶裝辣根醬開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 3～4 個月。未開封從購買日起算大約 12 個月。
要。它本來就是冷藏販售的商品，未開封和開封後都要冰。
嗆味成分是揮發性的，會隨時間散失，開封後更快，放在溫暖處又更快。
沒有對應期限，效果也不好——冷凍會讓嗆味散掉，只剩出水的糊。建議改冰一整條辣根現磨。
